To the forest-dwelling seer,
long practiced in austerity,
mature and developed in self,
I gave a sandal as a gift.
By that deed, O Lord of Bipeds,
Supreme One in the World, Bull among Men;
I experience a divine vehicle;
this is the fruit of my former karma.
Ninety-four aeons ago from now...
Whatever deed I performed back then,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of that gift of water.
In the seventy-seventh aeon,
there were eight kshatriyas known by the name Suyāna.
Universal monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Pānadhidāyaka recited these verses.
This is the second apadāna of the elder Pānadhidāyaka.
